body.statement: Starting from the constant-\(X\) finite-feature inverse \(\mathfrak I_0\), can the handle \(\mathfrak I\) be completed into a conditional-\(X\), measurable, uniformly bounded right inverse from every observed DQM score in \(\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\) to centered latent additive factor scores, including support-preserving recovery of the full class-density score?
body.justification: This is the non-formal consequence of tensor identification on which the claimed canonicality genuinely rests.
body.gap: Hu and Schennach identify a continuous latent full law under operator conditions, and Deaner transports that recovery to triple-proxy causal functionals; these level-identification results do not differentiate the factorization or furnish a conditional-\(X\), measurable, uniformly bounded right inverse for every observed DQM score. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes establish discrete factor uniqueness, while Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen project oracle scores in the binary model.
body.consumer: A positive answer certifies that no unmodeled observed tangent direction invalidates the efficiency bound; a negative answer kills the canonical-gradient spine.
